I damn near choked on my turkey and mashed potatoes when that came out of her mouth. DING. DING. DING. It was exactly what I was thinking as I was driving down I-75 south to Dayton. It felt like just another day on the highway. I've been driving this same route for 30 years and yesterday was easily the busiest with truck traffic that I'd ever seen.

item.title: Bob Newhart faced $6M lawsuit threat after trying to quit hit sitcom: book
item.description: CBS threatened Bob Newhart with a $6 million lawsuit when he tried to quit "The Bob Newhart Show" before its sixth season, a new biography reveals.
item.content:encoded:
Bob Newhart could make millions laugh, but a $6 million lawsuit was no laughing matter.

The comedy legend once tried to quit his hit CBS sitcom, "The Bob Newhart Show," only to discover the network wasn't ready to let its ratings star walk away.

The contract dispute is detailed in Michael Seth Starr's biography, "Bob Newhart: The Life and Laughter of an American Treasure," which chronicles the comedian's nearly 65-year career.

BOB NEWHART, LEGENDARY COMEDIAN AND SITCOM STAR, DEAD AT 94

Newhart wasn't exactly in a position to face a multimillion-dollar lawsuit.

"I don't have $6 million," the comedian later admitted. "And my wife wouldn't lend me any of her money."

Although he publicly credited fan support for his decision, Newhart later acknowledged that financial pressure played a major role in his return.

"When I said I wanted to quit, the people in the cast and the production crew were all affected, of course and they helped influence me to change my mind. Then there were letters from fans and people I met on the street. But I guess the main reason I decided to come back was that CBS threatened to sue me for $6 million because there was a year left on my contract."

According to Starr's biography, Newhart approached CBS executives Bob Daly and Robert Wussler about leaving "The Bob Newhart Show" before its sixth season.

His attorney warned that if a replacement series failed to generate comparable revenue, CBS could seek damages Newhart estimated at "about fifty or sixty million dollars."

The comedian also questioned the show's creative future, with head writers Tom Patchett and Jay Tarses occupied with other projects.

"So, I thought maybe five years was enough. I'd rather go off a year early than a year late," he recalled. He hoped to negotiate television specials instead, saying, "I'd rather do specials, even if it means walking away from a lot of money."

CBS ultimately convinced him to return for a sixth and final season, with Starr describing concessions that included better scripts, flexibility to miss one or two episodes and "a modest bump" in his $30,000-per-episode salary.

'MARY TYLER MOORE' STAR ED ASNER SAYS CAST WAS LIKE A FAMILY: 'WE FORGAVE EACH OTHER'S FAULTS'

CBS executive Robert Wussler later recalled Newhart telling him and Daly, "You can sue me and take me to court."

Wussler recalled their response: "Wait a minute — we don't want to sue you. We just want you back."

Newhart eventually agreed, recalling, "Both ["The Mary Tyler Moore Show"] MTM and CBS were so darned nice to me, I got to thinking: 'Why not go ahead with another year?'"

He added, "What’s so tough about it? People were already starting to say I was quitting because I wouldn’t have ["The Mary Tyler Moore Show"] anymore as a lead-in, which was nonsense."

Newhart ultimately returned for the final season, which ended in 1978. He went on to star in another hit CBS sitcom, "Newhart," which ran from 1982 to 1990.

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

He later won his first competitive Emmy in 2013 for his guest role as Arthur Jeffries on "The Big Bang Theory."

Newhart was married to his wife, Ginnie, for 60 years before she died in April 2023. The couple had four children together.

During an appearance on "Nostalgia Tonight with Joe Sibilia," Starr spoke about their relationship and how Ginnie's death affected Newhart.

"He and Ginnie were so close, and I think losing her was just such a big blow. And I mean, he had been slowing down in the last maybe five or six years of his life. I interviewed him maybe about a year and a half or two years before he passed away. And he didn't sound great. He was coughing a lot, and he sounded a little weak, but he was in his 90s."

"I mean, he did live a very long life and very fruitful life," he noted of Newhart. "And we're still talking about him now, and I think people will be talking about him for years and years after this. So he certainly left his mark on the American public and the American consciousness."

WATCH: BOB NEWHART SUFFERED ‘BROKEN HEART SYNDROME’ AFTER WIFE DIED: AUTHOR

Newhart died July 18, 2024, at his Los Angeles home at age 94, following a series of short illnesses. His family was by his side.

His career spanned more than six decades, from his Grammy-winning 1960 comedy album "The Button-Down Mind of Bob Newhart" to two iconic sitcoms and a memorable late-career television comeback.

item.title: Nature video captures elk fending off two wolves in a dramatic animal fight caught on camera

item.content:encoded:

item.title: US pilot tells Trump which fighter jet is ‘world’s greatest’ during Thanksgiving phone call
item.description: An F-16 pilot told President Donald Trump the jet is the "world's greatest" during a Thanksgiving call, saying "you couldn't pay me to switch airplanes."
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump learned what the "world's greatest" fighter jet is, according to an F-16 pilot, during a phone call on Thanksgiving Day.

"So could I ask, before I give my little speech to you — a little quick one — could I ask, so the F-16, you love it, right?" Trump asked U.S. Air Force Lt. Col. Brant Smith.

"World's greatest fighter jet, sir," Smith replied.

Trump spoke to Smith from his Mar-a-Lago resort in Florida as the president and first lady Melania made calls to service members from all six branches of the U.S. military.

A LOOK AT HOW THE TRUMPS SPEND THEIR THANKSGIVING HOLIDAY THROUGH THE YEARS

Trump asked Smith to compare his F-16 to other fighter jets like the F-22 or F-35, to which Smith replied: "The F-16 all day."

TRUMP SAYS AIR FORCE PILOTS DESCRIBED A ROUND UFO FLYING THREE TIMES FASTER THAN AN F-22 FIGHTER JET

"You couldn't pay me to switch airplanes," Smith added.

"I love flying this airplane. And I think there are very few pilots in this room that would argue with me. Both of those airplanes (F-22 and F-35) are great, and they have their place in the world and in the war. But, this is a lot of fun. We get to do it all, and it does it all very well," Smith said.

The president also asked Smith about his service and queried about what he was doing at the time.

"We are pre-installing the air base in Saudi Arabia," Smith replied.

CENTCOM'S THANKSGIVING MESSAGE TO TROOPS 'IS ONE OF DEEP GRATITUDE' FOR THEIR 'EXCEPTIONAL WORK' PROTECTING US

"You have a pretty large crowd of pilots, maintainers and ops support personnel from the 510th Expeditionary Fighter Squadron, the Buzzards. We're an F-16 unit. We've been on here since about ten days before Epic Fury kicked off. And we're flying combat operations out in the straits every day," he continued.

Trump complimented Smith on the military's efforts in the Middle East and in the war with Iran.

TRUMP PAUSES TURKEY PARDON TO SALUTE US TROOPS GUARDING STRAIT OF HORMUZ: 'WATCH OVER AND PROTECT'

"And you're seeing some big victories, aren't you? Knocking them out left and right, knocking out the launchers, knocking out the missiles, knocking out left and right. Amazing job you're doing, Brant," Trump said.

"Thank you, sir," the airman responded.

TRUMP SAYS IRAN UNLEASHED MISSILE, DRONE SURGE AFTER MIDTERMS

Smith also told the president he believes Iran was "starting to run out of things." Trump concurred.

"Yep. I think they are. I think they are. And that'll continue. And we're getting stronger. We sent an extra aircraft carrier," Trump said, referring to the Nimitz-class USS Theodore Roosevelt, which arrived in the Middle East on Nov. 16 to relieve USS George Washington.

US RACES TO BUILD BUNKERS ACROSS MIDDLE EAST AS IRANIAN STRIKES THREATEN AMERICAN TROOPS

"In my opinion, they're not very smart. They're making big mistakes. They've made a lot of mistakes. Their economy is down the tubes," the president said of Iran.

"Every day the stellar F-16 squadron is conducting missions across the Middle East to defend our interests and our assets. Like few people could ever even think about. This year, you've flown more than 2,000 sorties over more than 12,000 hours across eight different operations, including Operation Epic Fury. And you're getting plenty of time out there, aren't you, Brant?"

"Yes, sir," Smith said, adding, "Nine months and 10 days."

"And you love it, right?" Trump asked.

"Yeah, we're having fun," Smith said. "This is what we trained for."

"Amazing. The best in the world," Trump replied.

item.title: George Kittle 'really should be a part of' WWE when he done in the NFL, 49ers star says

Kittle, who entered the building with Penta’s mask on his head, hit the Lucha Libre star’s "Cero Miedo" celebration when he scored his first touchdown. He finished with two on the night.

"As a kid, I loved WWE. Me and my brothers, we would have our own WWE matches in the living room. We’d set up the cushions from the couches on the floor," he said. "We’d powerbomb each other into the sofa and stuff. I loved it as a kid. So, I definitely have an appreciation for that.

"And I love that George is so into it and he embodies that WWE character. He really should be a part of it when he’s done playing football. I love, not only that he loves WWE, but he’s still such a big kid at heart. That’s truly one of the things I love most about George. He keeps the child alive in all of us."

"I love Penta. He's awesome," he said. "I met Penta like eight or nine years ago. I watched him wrestle like five different times for five different companies. It was awesome. And then the following year, I got to meet him, did a jersey swap with him, and we just kind of been in contact ever since.

"I completely took his ‘Cero Miedo’ because I think it's just, I like the confidence that it exudes. And I just think he's an awesome wrestler. I'm so happy that he's in the WWE now. It's really fun."

Kittle did get involved in a match once. He gave The Miz a clothesline at WrestleMania 39, allowing Pat McAfee to pick up a victory.

item.title: Wife of Patrick Mahomes unleashes fire and fury towards refs after botched call in Buffalo
item.description: Tyler Bass drilled a field goal after a blocked punt lifted the Buffalo Bills past the Kansas City Chiefs 13-10 in a Thanksgiving football thriller.
item.content:encoded:
Thursday delivered us quite possibly the greatest slate of Thanksgiving football games of all time, and it ended with a bang.

Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills stunned the Kansas City Chiefs at the buzzer, 13-10, thanks in large part to a blocked punt in the waning seconds. The Bills deflected the kick, it was returned by Greg Dortch to Kansas City's 39, and Tyler Bass drilled the long field goal to walk it off.

It was the perfect day of football — including two stunning comebacks in Detroit and Dallas. Again, I'd argue it was the greatest Thanksgiving slate ever.

BUFFALO BILLS OUTLAST KANSAS CITY CHIEFS IN DEFENSIVE STRUGGLE TO MAINTAIN TOP SEED STATUS IN AFC

Of course — because we can't have nice things — it didn't come without some controversy at the end. In another stunning turn of events, this one actually worked against the Chiefs!

That's right. Rashee Rice had a catch overturned late in the fourth quarter that took away a Kansas City first down, even though it certainly looked like a catch. The refs looked it over, decided it didn't count, and forced the Chiefs to punt instead.

You rarely see a call go against the Chiefs. It's been a running joke amongst NFL fans for years now. So, yes, seeing one screw them over was a stunner.

Don't take my word for it, though! Just ask Brittany Mahomes, the firecracker wife of star QB Patrick Mahomes:

"Guess we can't even play football without it getting called against us," Mahomes said, via her Instagram story after the game. "Not sure what an actual catch is after that I guess? I don't wanna hear s–t anymore from anyone."

Incredible. Again, seeing a call go against the Chiefs was shocking. You just don't see it. You haven't seen it during the Mahomes era. Not saying I agree with the call, by the way, because I'm not sure I do.

I think it was probably a catch. It was ruled that way on the field, so I'm not sure how they would overturn it based on that video evidence. I just don't see that ball move. Even Mike Tirico had to squint to see it.

THE ABSOLUTE WORST CALL OF THE COLLEGE FOOTBALL SEASON HAPPENED LAST NIGHT WHILE YOU WERE SLEEPING

If that's not a catch, I'm not sure what we're doing anymore. And I'm not a Chiefs fan, believe me. I don't love defending them here, but fair is fair, and that was probably a bogus reversal.

Par the course for the refs, though. They've been HORRIBLE this week. They screwed over the Jags in New York on Sunday, then awarded Mike Evans a fake touchdown Sunday night, and then completely botched a call in Tuesday's MACtion game between Kent State and Eastern Michigan.

And now, they have me defending the Kansas City Chiefs and Brittany Mahomes!

What a time to be alive.

What a week.

item.title: Treasure hunters searching a field uncover 5,500-coin hoard hiding 'national treasure'
item.description: Archaeologist Anne Skogsfjord spotted the rare Saint Olaf coin inside Norway's largest Viking Age hoard, the first such find there since 1924, officials said.
item.content:encoded:
Archaeologists in Norway have uncovered an extraordinarily rare 1,000-year-old coin minted during the reign of Viking King Olaf Haraldsson, better known as Saint Olaf, inside the largest Viking Age coin hoard ever found in the country.

The discovery, announced by the Museum of Cultural History in Oslo, marks the first time a coin of this type has been found in Norway since 1924.

The Olaf coin went on display Nov. 20 at the Historical Museum in Oslo — part of the University of Oslo's Museum of Cultural History — as part of a new exhibition showcasing the Mørstad Hoard.

PUZZLING SOUND IN BACKYARD LEADS HOMEOWNER TO MASSIVE 1,000-YEAR-OLD TREASURE

The hoard was originally discovered on April 10 by metal detectorists Vegard Sørlie and Rune Sætre in Rena, Innlandet County, and the site has since been secured and investigated for further research.

Officials said the latest count puts the cache at 5,500 coins, though researchers believe the total could soon exceed 6,000.

The star of the hoard, officials said, is a coin depicting Haraldsson, who ruled from 1015 to 1028.

Haraldsson, who became a saint after his death, occupies "a unique place in Norwegian history," officials said.

RARE COIN BEARING FACE OF KING WITH INFAMOUS NICKNAME UNEARTHED AFTER 1,000 YEARS

"Fewer than 20 of his coins have survived to the present day, and most have been found outside Norway," the release said.

"Only four examples of the type found in the Mørstad Hoard have previously been discovered, including just one in Norway."

The new coin was spotted by archaeologist Anne Skogsfjord, who immediately ran to tell a colleague about the find.

Officials said the coin was initially thought to be Anglo-Saxon and had been roughly sorted into the group of coins issued by Æthelred II.

MYSTERIOUS FIND BENEATH FIELD LEADS MAN TO MASSIVE TREASURE HIDDEN FOR CENTURIES

"I could see that it read ONLAF R+ NORMANORV … Could this really be a coin of Olaf Haraldsson that I was holding?" Skogsfjord said. "And it was! It was a very special moment."

She added, "I realized that we had found a national treasure."

The coin dates between 1024 and 1028, and officials said it may have been in circulation for up to 25 years before it was deposited in the hoard.

Featuring a cross on both sides, the coin shows how Olaf used currency to legitimize the Christian faith and establish himself as a Christian king of European standing, according to numismatics expert Svein H. Gullbekk.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

The museum added, "Few archaeological and historical sources can be directly linked to Olaf Haraldsson himself. Numismatic sources — the coins — were closely connected to the king."

Gullbekk said in the release, "Olaf Haraldsson himself decided what these coins should look like, and perhaps he was present when they were struck. It is entirely possible that this very coin from Mørstad was once held in the king's own hand." 

Hanna Geiran, Norway's director general of cultural heritage, said the coin "is not only a rare object, but also tangible testimony from a time when the foundations of the Norwegian kingdom and the Christianization of the country were laid."

"When you think this Viking treasure cannot become any more exciting, new surprises emerge," said Geiran, the museum noted.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

"This St. Olaf coin is yet another reminder of how extraordinary this find is."

Looking ahead, the museum said that research on the coin hoard will continue "for a long time to come."

"Every single coin must undergo the same thorough process before entering the museum collection," added officials. "Numismatists, archaeologists, conservators, collection managers and photographers are all involved."

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

The Mørstad Hoard joins several other significant European coin discoveries unearthed in recent months.

Earlier this year, archaeologists in Germany uncovered 11 ancient Celtic coins at a construction site — the largest hoard of its kind ever found in the region, dating back more than 2,000 years.

Meanwhile, in Finland, a metal detectorist recently unearthed a Viking Age silver cache holding around 4,000 coins, jewelry and other artifacts.

item.description: Josh Holloway recalls Kevin Costner calling his own take "lazy" on the "Yellowstone" set, revealing the high standards the star kept through season five.
item.content:encoded:
Josh Holloway is pulling back the curtain on what life was like on the set of "Yellowstone."

The neo-Western series created by Taylor Sheridan dominated TV for all five of its seasons. The success of Sheridan's crowning achievement also led to multiple prequels and spinoffs.

The "Yellowstone" universe is a powerhouse, and Holloway played a major role. He starred as villain Roarke Morris in season three of the series, and very briefly appeared in season four.

LUKE GRIMES SAYS HE HASN'T SPOKEN TO KEVIN COSTNER SINCE 'YELLOWSTONE'

Now, he's shining a light on what Kevin Costner was like on set, and the high standards and work ethic the legendary actor brought to the series.

Holloway recently appeared on the "Inside of You" podcast hosted by Michael Rosenbaum, and explained that Costner wasn't afraid to call himself out on set when he didn't perform at a high level.

ZOE SALDAÑA SAYS TAYLOR SHERIDAN GIVES STARS TWO CHOICES: 'MAKE SURE THAT YOU DON'T F--K UP... OR YOU QUIT'

"What I was impressed with with him, he did a close-up with me where he’s telling me about the rules or something, and he did it, and he just went inside and he was like, ‘Ah, that sh*t was lazy.’ And then he came up and I was like, ‘He cares. He’s still working.’ And he brought it. He's in this. So, I was impressed with that. You know, that he’s still keeping his standard high. I respected that. I was like, ‘Hell yeah,'" Holloway explained.

You can watch Holloway's comments in the video below starting around 1:05:00, and let me know your thoughts at David.Hookstead@outkick.com.

'YELLOWSTONE' STAR NEAL MCDONOUGH REFUSES TO WATCH HIT SERIES FOR ‘PAINFUL’ REASON

It's worth noting that while Costner might have held himself to extremely high standards on set, his time on "Yellowstone" didn't end in great fashion.

Costner infamously split from the show during the mid-season split in season five, and never returned to ever play John Dutton again.

His exit, which led to plenty of reports of feuds behind the scenes, resulted in the final "Yellowstone" episodes feeling a bit rushed and an ending that never truly felt complete.

Don't get me wrong. The conclusion of "Yellowstone" was always clear to anyone paying attention, but without John Dutton, something just felt a little unsatisfied.

item.title: Google Gemini may expose private emails to reviewers
item.description: A researcher claims Google Gemini pulled private Gmail billing details into chats, and Google confirms some connected-app data may face human review.
item.content:encoded:
Think about everything sitting in your Gmail inbox right now. Maybe there's a conversation with your doctor, a recent bank statement or a personal message you never intended anyone else to read. Your Google Drive may hold years of private documents. You probably don't spend much time thinking about who might see that information beyond the people you share it with. But what happens when you connect those services to Google's Gemini AI assistant?

An independent researcher has raised concerns about how Gemini handles information retrieved from connected Gmail and Google Drive accounts. The findings prompted questions about whether some private content could end up in conversations reviewed by humans.

We contacted Google, and the company confirmed that some information retrieved from connected Gmail and Drive accounts may be seen by human reviewers under certain circumstances. Google stressed that these connections are off by default. Here's what you should know before giving Gemini access to your personal information.

Missed CyberGuy LIVE? Watch the replay and discover 5 ways to travel smarter and save money.

Our free CyberGuy LIVE class, 5 Ways to Travel Smarter and Save Money, has ended, but you can still watch the full replay. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you through five practical ways to protect your phone and personal information, avoid common travel scams, find better deals, save money on bookings and use technology to make your travels easier and less stressful. No technical experience is needed.

Watch the free replay + downloadable checklist now at CyberGuyLive.com.

AI CHATBOT PRIVACY: WHAT YOUR AI MAY KNOW ABOUT YOU

An independent researcher using the name thisisme6598 published findings on GitHub, raising questions about the way Gemini retrieves information from connected Gmail and Google Drive accounts. The researcher tested Gemini using a personal Google Account with connected apps enabled. According to the published findings, Gemini sometimes retrieved information from emails or files during conversations without someone explicitly asking it to search Gmail or Drive. For example, the researcher described asking Gemini whether an internet service bill seemed too expensive. During some tests, Gemini reportedly retrieved billing information from Gmail, including payment amounts, account details and confirmation numbers.

In certain instances, the researcher reported that Gemini returned several sentences directly from an email and, in some tests, the entire email, including its headers. The researcher argues that this behavior creates a privacy concern because information retrieved into a Gemini conversation may become eligible for human review. However, the published findings do not establish that a human reviewer actually accessed the researcher's emails. Google told CyberGuy that the reported retrieval was standard behavior for someone who had voluntarily connected their apps. The company also emphasized that retrieved files remain visible only to the authenticated account holder and are not exposed publicly through this process.

Yes, under certain circumstances. Google's own Connected Apps privacy documentation confirms that trained human reviewers, including service providers, may review a subset of information processed through Gemini's connected apps. That information can include summaries or excerpts from relevant Gmail messages and Google Drive documents.

In some cases, Google acknowledges that reviewers may see a complete email or file if it is short or especially relevant to the request. Google also says human reviewers may access some Gmail inbox content when investigating abuse or harm or responding to submitted feedback.

The company uses these reviews to evaluate Gemini's responses and improve its services.

Simply using Gmail or Google Drive does not subject your private content to this review process. The concern involves information retrieved after someone voluntarily connects those services to consumer Gemini. Google says it does not train generative AI models directly on someone's entire Gmail inbox or Drive. However, relevant information processed during Gemini conversations may be used for model improvement, depending on account settings. Google specifically warns against connecting apps containing confidential information someone would be uncomfortable having a reviewer see.

We contacted Google directly to ask whether human reviewers could access Gmail messages or Drive files processed through the consumer Gemini app. We also asked whether the company had changed its privacy disclosures, notified existing customers and provided ways to prevent human review. A Google spokesperson told CyberGuy:

"Gmail and Google Drive’s core privacy protections remain unchanged, and your private emails and files are not reviewed by humans simply by using Gmail, Drive, or built-in Workspace features. Connecting those apps to the consumer Gemini app is off by default — it’s an optional way to get more personalized, time-saving answers across your Google apps when you want them. Users can disconnect their apps in Gemini settings at any time without losing access to Gemini’s core features."

Google also confirmed that when someone connects their apps to consumer Gemini with activity saving enabled, a small subset of conversations may undergo human review. Those conversations can contain relevant information retrieved from connected services. Before trained service providers review the material, Google says it separates the conversations from the associated Google Account and takes steps to reduce identifying information. The company also disputes the suggestion that the researcher's findings demonstrate public exposure of private files.

Another part of the controversy involves changes to Google's public privacy disclosures. In Oct. 2023, Google published a blog post about its approach to generative AI privacy. The company said that content from Gmail, Docs and Drive accessed through Bard's Workspace extensions would not be seen by human reviewers or used to train the Bard model.

On Oct. 16, 2026, Google added an update to that same blog post. The new language explains that Google has introduced additional optional features allowing people to connect Workspace information to other Google services. Google says that when someone enables these newer features, a subset of the information may be used to train generative AI models, depending on their settings. It may also undergo human review in limited circumstances. The researcher argues that the change represents a reversal of Google's earlier privacy commitment.

However, Google's original statement concerned Bard's Workspace extensions, while the updated disclosure addresses newer connected features. The available evidence does not establish that Google quietly changed the underlying handling of information in existing connections. We asked Google whether people who previously connected their accounts were notified about the updated disclosures or asked to provide additional consent. Google's response did not directly address those questions. Instead, the company emphasized that the newer connections are optional and can be disabled. That leaves an important question about how clearly Google communicates changes to its AI privacy practices, particularly as new features gain access to more personal information.

APPLE TIGHTENS MAC SECURITY AS AI AGENTS SEEK YOUR FILES

Google says it disconnects conversations from the associated Google Account before sending them to trained service providers for routine review. The company also takes steps to reduce personal information. However, removing account identifiers does not necessarily eliminate every sensitive detail contained in an email excerpt or document summary.

Google's Gemini Apps Privacy Hub explains that conversations reviewed by service providers may be retained for up to three years, even after someone deletes the corresponding activity from their Google Account.

Turning off Gemini's History setting, previously called Keep Activity, prevents future conversations from being used to train generative AI models unless someone submits feedback. However, Google may still process conversations for security and safety purposes, including with help from human reviewers.

On Nov. 16, 2026, Google announced changes to its Gemini privacy controls. Under the previous policy, Google retained conversations for up to 72 hours when Keep Activity was turned off. Under the new policy, Google will retain conversations for approximately two months when History is turned off. The company is rolling out these changes globally over several weeks.

If you use Gemini, it's worth checking which accounts and services you've connected. You may find that you don't need every feature enabled. Here are some settings worth reviewing.

Google groups Gmail and Drive under Google Workspace in its connected-app settings. Here's how to check the connection on a computer.

If you see a different menu, look for Connected Apps in Gemini's settings. Google offers different connection controls depending on account eligibility and available features. You can reconnect supported services later if you decide to use them.

If you want to prevent future conversations from being used to train Google's generative AI models, review this setting.

Turning off History stops future chats from being used to train generative AI models unless you choose to submit feedback. Some connected apps, including Google Workspace, become unavailable. Google may still process conversations for security and safety purposes. Depending on whether the latest privacy update has reached your account, conversations may be retained for up to 72 hours under the previous policy or approximately two months under the new policy.

WHAT YOUR INTERNET PROVIDER, WEBSITES AND ADVERTISERS SEE

Google is introducing a separate privacy control that lets you keep your Gemini conversation history while opting out of generative AI model training. If the new setting is available on your account, here's how to find it on a computer.

Google says future chats will no longer be used to train generative AI models unless you submit feedback. However, human review may still occur for other service improvements and safety purposes. If you want to prevent Gemini from retrieving information from Gmail and Drive, disconnect Google Workspace separately.

Disconnecting an app does not automatically delete information from earlier Gemini conversations. Google says Gemini may still use information from previously saved chats even after you disconnect the original app. That's why it's important to both disconnect the app and delete conversations containing sensitive information.

Remember that previously reviewed information may remain subject to Google's separate retention policies, even after you delete your activity.

Think carefully before giving an AI assistant access to confidential documents or personal communications. If you don't need Gemini to retrieve information from Gmail or Drive, leave those connections disabled. Also, remember that uploading a document directly into Gemini creates a separate privacy consideration.

Google says uploaded content may be used to improve its services when History, previously called Keep Activity, is enabled, potentially with help from human reviewers. Whether that content is used to train generative AI models also depends on your training settings and whether you submit feedback.

Google says the connected-app disclosures involved in this controversy apply to personal Google Accounts using consumer Gemini. Business, Enterprise and Education accounts covered by Google Workspace commercial terms have different privacy protections. According to Google's response to CyberGuy, customer data governed by those commercial terms is not reviewed by humans or used to train foundational AI models.

If you use Gemini through an employer or school, your organization's settings and agreements determine which features are available and how information is handled. The important point is that the consumer Gemini privacy rules discussed here should not automatically be applied to commercial Workspace accounts.

I can understand why someone would want Gemini to search their Gmail or find a document buried in Google Drive. We've all wasted time digging through old emails looking for something we need. Having an AI assistant do that work sounds pretty appealing. But I think Google has a responsibility to make the privacy implications much clearer before someone connects an account. Most people probably don't expect information pulled from their private emails to become part of a conversation that could eventually be reviewed by another human being. I appreciate that Google responded to our questions and explained the safeguards it uses. Still, I would have liked a more direct answer about whether existing customers were notified when the privacy disclosures changed. If you're giving an AI assistant access to years of personal information, you deserve to know exactly how that information might be handled. Personally, I'd leave Gmail and Drive disconnected unless I had a specific reason to use those features.

Would you trust an AI assistant with access to years of your private emails if you knew some of that information could be seen by human reviewers? Or has Google crossed a privacy line, even with your permission? Let us know by writing to us at Cyberguy.com.

item.title: From Hollywood mogul to Biden-Harris insiders, Democrats turn to familiar faces to shape their next chapter
item.description: Abdul El-Sayed's transition team director previously claimed Zionists were "controlling" U.S. politics, while Tyler Perry co-chairs Georgia's team.
item.content:encoded:
On the heels of the blue wave in the 2026 U.S. midterms, incoming Democratic leaders are tapping an eclectic mix of political veterans, business executives and entertainment figures to help shape their transitions into power.

From a Hollywood mogul and former Biden administration officials to figures with ties to Republican leaders, the appointments offer an early glimpse into the people Democrats are turning to as they prepare to govern — and the experience and connections they hope to bring into their new administrations.

Several incoming Democrats are turning to familiar faces from the Biden administration. In New Mexico, Gov.-elect Deb Haaland tapped former Biden presidential speechwriter Felicia Salazar and former Interior Department official Joan Mooney for her transition team, while California Gov.-elect Xavier Becerra selected Arsenio Mataka, who previously served as his senior counselor at the Department of Health and Human Services under Biden, to direct policy for his transition team. In Ohio, Democratic Gov.-elect Amy Acton tapped Elisabeth Hire, a former aide to then-Vice President Biden, as a transition co-chair.

Haaland's campaign and Becerra's campaign each did not respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.

The transition teams will help incoming leaders prepare to take office, including identifying potential administration officials, shaping policy priorities and laying the groundwork for their first days in power. The selections also offer a window into the experience, relationships and perspectives newly elected Democrats are turning to as they prepare to govern.

Sen.-elect Abdul El-Sayed, D-Mich., tapped Egyptian-American lawyer Brenda Abdelall as the director of his transition team, Politico Playbook first reported in early November. Abdelall previously claimed that Zionists were "controlling" much of U.S. politics, The Washington Free Beacon reported Nov. 6, though Harris' 2024 presidential campaign said at the time that the remarks did not reflect Abdelall's current views.

"The Zionists have a strong voice in American politics," Abdelall told the New York Sun during a conference for the American Muslim Council in 2002, the Free Beacon reported. "I would say they're controlling a lot of it."

Abdelall previously served as the assistant secretary of partnership and engagement at the U.S. Department of Homeland Security. She also directed the Kamala Harris 2024 presidential campaign's outreach to Arab American voters, Reuters reported.

JEWISH LEADERS IN MICHIGAN PREPARE TO WORK WITH ABDUL EL-SAYED DESPITE LINGERING CONCERNS

El-Sayed campaign spokesperson Roxie Richner told Fox News Digital on Nov. 9 that Abdelall "comes to the role of transition director with decades of experience leading teams at the highest levels of politics, including the Biden-Harris administration."

"While at the Department of Homeland Security, Brenda worked to implement the nation’s first National Strategy to Counter Antisemitism and frequently spearheaded efforts to counter the rise of hate crimes and violence across the country," Richner added. "The transition team is committed to building a team that reflects the great diversity of Michigan and ensuring that the El-Sayed office serves all communities across the state."

El-Sayed is set to assume office on Jan. 3, 2027.

DEMOCRATIC SENATOR-ELECT CALLS TRUMP 'UNSERIOUS FOOL' WHILE DEFENDING COMBATIVE POLITICAL STYLE

DEMOCRATS SEIZE MAJORITY OF GOVERNORS’ OFFICES IN ELECTION-NIGHT SHIFT

Democratic Georgia Gov.-elect Keisha Lance Bottoms announced Nov. 6 that filmmaker and actor Tyler Perry would serve as one of 10 co-chairs of her transition team, dubbed "Georgia's Promise," WBAL-TV reported. Perry has long been known for his philanthropic efforts, including supporting underserved communities and charitable causes across Georgia. Bottoms lauded Perry as "an entertainment mogul who is also a huge philanthropic part of our Georgia community and owns Tyler Perry Studios in Atlanta," WDSU reported.

EX-BIDEN OFFICIAL WINS GEORGIA DEM PRIMARY FOR GOVERNOR IN BID TO END PARTY'S LOSING STREAK

The news that Perry will serve on Bottoms’ Georgia transition team has sparked some criticism due to the entertainment mogul facing two active lawsuits accusing him of sexual assault and misconduct, allegations his attorneys have denied, Variety reported Nov. 6.

Perry has denied all sexual assault and harassment allegations made against him, People reported on March 3.

Maxscene, a division of Tyler Perry Studios, did not respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.

Bottoms previously was an executive producer on Netflix’s "Miss Governor," a 2025 political comedy sitcom produced by Tyler Perry Studios, per online film database IMDb.

Other prominent figures that have been tapped for Bottoms' transition committee include Home Depot co-founder Arthur Blank and former CEO of Walgreens Boots Alliance Roz Brewer, WBAL-TV reported.

Bottoms’ campaign did not respond to Fox News Digital’s request for comment.

Bottoms is set to take office on Jan. 11, 2027.

Democratic Attorney General-elect Nathan Johnson's transition team includes Mark Penley, a former deputy attorney general who reported outgoing Republican Attorney General Ken Paxton to the FBI, and Erin Epley, who served as lead attorney in Paxton's impeachment, The Houston Chronicle reported Nov. 16.

Johnson also tapped Amanda Crawford, a former appointee of Republican Gov. Greg Abbott, and Thaddeus Cleveland, a Republican sheriff from Terrell County, as part of his transition team, according to the Chronicle.

Johnson's campaign did not respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.

Democratic Gov.-elect David Crowley is also turning to the world of professional sports, tapping Alex Lasry, a former senior vice president of the NBA's Milwaukee Bucks, to serve on his transition team, Wisconsin Public Radio reported Nov. 11.

Lasry, the son of former Bucks co-owner and billionaire businessman Marc Lasry, helped oversee the franchise's operations during its rise to the 2021 NBA championship and played a key role in developing Milwaukee's Fiserv Forum arena. He also mounted an unsuccessful bid for the Democratic U.S. Senate nomination in 2022.

Crowley's campaign did not respond to Fox News Digital’s request for comment.

item.title: Supplements in the spotlight as longevity doctor shares his personal daily routine
item.description: Dr. Kien Vuu shares his daily supplement stack, from creatine and NMN to glutathione, each supporting muscle health, cellular energy and longevity.
item.content:encoded:
Nearly eight in 10 Americans take at least one dietary supplement for their health, according to a September 2026 Pew Research Center survey — yet clinicians warn that routine supplementation isn't always necessary or safe.

Dr. Kien Vuu, a Los Angeles-based physician specializing in longevity and author of the book "Thrive State," spoke to Fox News Digital about the role supplements play in overall health.

"Supplements are a signal," he told Fox News Digital during an event at Soft Bar + Cafe in Brooklyn, New York. "How we live life are signals. How we eat, how we sleep, how we move, how we connect with people, they're all signals to the body — and supplements can play a very important role."

DOCTOR'S 10 RULES FOR LIVING LONGER, CELEBRATING MORE BIRTHDAYS AND MAKING EXTRA YEARS COUNT

Certain supplements can support muscle growth, metabolism and cellular energy, but they work best when they're paired with "lifestyle choices and targeted support," the expert said.

Vuu, a partner with longevity and supplement brand Solaray, shared the supplements he takes on a daily basis.

Creatine, an amino acid-based compound, has become popular among fitness enthusiasts, as it has been shown to aid in boosting energy during exercise. The supplement is "really important" for muscle health and recovery, Vuu said.

COMMON GYM SUPPLEMENT COULD HELP FIGHT DEPRESSION, NEW RESEARCH SUGGESTS

The supplement has also demonstrated cognitive benefits, assisting with memory and processing speed, according to the National Institutes of Health.

Combining creatine with an MBP (milk basic protein) — a whey protein fraction studied for supporting bone formation and reducing bone breakdown — can support both muscle energy and bone health, according to Vuu.

NMN, short for nicotinamide mononucleotide, is a compound the body uses to make NAD+ — a vital coenzyme that helps cells convert food into energy and repair damaged DNA.

ANTI-AGING SUPPLEMENTS TAKEN BY MILLIONS MAY UNDERMINE CANCER TREATMENT, STUDY WARNS

As a basic step in his longevity routine, Vuu said he typically takes NMN to support cellular energy as natural NAD+ levels decline with age — though independent researchers note that clinical evidence in humans is still emerging.

Glutathione, a tripeptide antioxidant produced naturally in cells, helps the liver detoxify harmful compounds and protects cells from oxidative damage caused by pollution, stress and aging, according to UCLA Health.

In the body, the compound also plays a vital role in supporting immune and liver function, protecting red blood cells from oxidative damage and facilitating amino acid transport across cell membranes.

"When I travel or get super stressed, I like to use glutathione," Vuu said. "I find myself and my nervous system behaving a lot better."

Vuu also takes several staples aimed at filling common nutritional gaps, including vitamin D, magnesium, a multivitamin and fish oil for omega-3 fatty acids.

DR OZ REVEALS 3 FREE WAYS TO BOOST YOUR HEALTH — NO MEDICATION REQUIRED

"What I see very deficient in people these days is vitamin D," he said. "Even if they're out in the sun, our bodies are using so much vitamin D, fighting against some of the stresses we have in life, that it's really low."

Data from the National Institutes of Health shows that roughly one-third of U.S. adults are clinically deficient in vitamin D, and factors like sunscreen, winter sunlight angles, varying skin tones and higher body fat can limit how much the body produces.

"Supplementing with [vitamin D] improves their hormones, it improves their energy, it improves their sex life, improves their immune system," Vuu said — though clinicians note those benefits typically apply to people correcting a true deficiency rather than those whose levels are already normal.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

The doctor said he also takes mitochondrial supplements such as ubiquinol — the active antioxidant form of CoQ10 — which supports cellular energy production and helps protect cells from oxidative damage.

While many people fall short on certain nutrients — or could benefit from targeted supplementation — it is possible to overdo it. Vuu said it's important to know your baseline health and to target your specific needs.

"If you're a person looking to supplement, go work with a physician first," he advised. "See where your labs are, see what symptoms you might be having, and then recognize what your goals are."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

"The sweet spot is knowing what you need, knowing what the baseline is, and then taking the targeted [approach] to support you … You're not supposed to take everything, and it's going to be different for everyone."

Vuu added that supplements clearly play an important role in how the body functions, noting that "our cells are energetically listening to everything."

item.title: TSA warns common Thanksgiving packing mistake could cause delays on the way home
item.description: The Transportation Security Administration notes that turkey, stuffing and pies can fly in carry-ons, but gravy and cranberry sauce must go in checked bags.
item.content:encoded:
Thanksgiving turkeys can fly in the overhead bin this holiday weekend — but the gravy will have to ride in cargo.

Ahead of what could be a more than 3-million-passenger rush nationwide on the Sunday after Thanksgiving, the Transportation Security Administration (TSA) is reminding travelers about which holiday foods and drinks can clear airport checkpoints and which ones belong in checked luggage.

Officials at Boston Logan International Airport, which is bracing for up to 77,000 travelers a day on Sunday and Monday, issued the reminder in an effort to keep security lines moving during the post-holiday surge.

TSA WARNS TRAVELERS ABOUT SEASONAL MISTAKE THAT COULD TRIGGER AIRPORT SECURITY DELAYS

The agency's rule of thumb comes down to solids versus liquids, with plenty of Thanksgiving staples falling on either side of the line.

All meats — turkey, ham and chicken, for example — are considered solids and are allowed in carry-on bags.

Passengers can also go through TSA with mac and cheese, stuffing, casseroles and fresh produce, including potatoes, yams, apples and cranberries.

Travelers hoping to bring Thanksgiving desserts on their trip are in luck as well.

TSA OFFICER SEES ALARMING SHAPES ON X-RAY BEFORE STOLEN CIVIL WAR MYSTERY UNRAVELS

Holiday pies, cakes, cookies and brownies are all permitted through checkpoints, according to the TSA in a news release. 

But plenty of the sides and sauces that go with Thanksgiving classics will have to go in checked luggage.

The list includes cranberry sauce — both homemade and commercially canned — as well as gravy, preserves and other canned goods, as long as the items are above 3.4 ounces.

"Slushy or partially melted ice packs will not be permitted through checkpoints," the TSA said. 

Anyone hoping to sneak prohibited items through security may have a tougher time this Thanksgiving weekend as well.

Officials said TSA is using real-time photo ID checks, automated bin lanes and 3D scanners at Boston Logan to inspect carry-on bags while letting travelers leave electronics and small liquids packed.

TSA Federal Security Director for Massachusetts Bob Allison said in the press release that officers "encourage travelers to give themselves plenty of time, review what is permitted in carry-on bags and arrive at the checkpoint prepared."

"These simple steps help our officers maintain strong security while keeping the passenger experience moving as efficiently as possible," added Allison.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Officials also encouraged Americans to check what is allowed before heading to the airport using the myTSA app or by reaching out to AskTSA online or via text message.

"Additionally, travelers should ensure that any ice packs used to keep holiday foods cold are completely frozen when passing through security," TSA noted.

"Slushy or partially melted ice packs will not be permitted through checkpoints."

item.content:encoded:

SHANE GILLIS WISHES EX-GIRLFRIEND 'THE BEST' AFTER TELL-ALL ESSAY ACCUSING HIM OF CHEATING AND 'RED FLAGS'

K-9 Spike, a 4-year-old Belgian Malinois, served with the Burbank Police Department for roughly two years and was wearing a ballistic vest when he was killed during a search for an armed suspect who ran from the stop.

In additional comments, Robinson argued that Spike never should have been forced into a life-threatening situation and claimed officers chose that fate for him. 

"F--- you dirty pigs," he wrote, later adding, "Trying to drum up emotion for a dog y’all forced to work. Classic dumb pig s---!" while calling out a specific officer by name.

After the remarks disappeared from the post, Robinson returned to the comments section to accuse the department of scrubbing his criticism, writing, "You took my comments down?!!!! What are you trying to hide pigs??!! What about transparency???"

A spokesperson for the Burbank Police Department denied removing Robinson’s remarks, telling Fox News Digital, "The Burbank Police Department does not delete comments from its social media posts. However, Instagram has its own policies and procedures that may automatically hide comments identified as derogatory, offensive, or otherwise in violation of the platform’s guidelines."

"Additionally, any Instagram user may report a comment they believe violates those guidelines, which may result in Instagram reviewing and hiding the content," the spokesperson added.

JIM GAFFIGAN, NEW YORK LAWMAKERS PUSH GOV HOCHUL TO AXE 'UNNECESSARY TAX' HITTING COMEDY CLUBS

The police department initially responded with a crying face emoji, prompting Robinson to reply, "maybe don’t constantly harass and brutalize the community!"

From there, the exchange continued with the department telling Robinson it is "open to discussion." He then posted a link to a FOX 11 Los Angeles report in which Aerin Robinson accused the Burbank Police Department of police brutality after his October 2025 arrest.

The arrest, captured on body camera video, showed a man with a bloodied face being struck with a stun gun. Aerin Robinson was initially stopped for suspected drug possession and resisting arrest. item.title: How to spot real Black Friday savings this holiday season amid the affordability squeeze

item.content:encoded:
Black Friday deals are everywhere, but a sale price does not always mean real savings.

With budgets under pressure, amid a persisting affordability crisis and rising fuel prices with the raging Iran conflict, shoppers are looking for ways to stretch their money during the holiday shopping season this year.

The forecasts point to a season of cautious spending. Visa Business and Economics Insights expects holiday sales to increase 4.5% from last year — but after accounting for higher prices, the actual increase in what shoppers buy is projected to be just 1.1%.

That makes it all the more important for shoppers to know what they’re paying for and whether a sale is truly a deal.

"It's still a good time to shop. It's just that you just have to be a little bit more careful," Dinesh Gauri, a marketing professor at the University at Buffalo, told Fox News Digital when discussing holiday and Black Friday shopping.

7 HOLIDAY SHOPPING SCAMS TO WATCH FOR THIS SEASON

Gauri revealed that shopping during Black Friday does not always produce the best deal — especially when it comes to essential technology like cell phones.

He advised shoppers to set a budget and research prices before making a purchase, especially for big-ticket items.

"Have a number in mind and do your research before you go about spending the money," he said, recommending price-tracking sites and extra promotions.

Gauri cited higher gas prices compared with last year as a potential pressure point for consumers, particularly those considering larger purchases.

While the average price of a gallon has risen from approximately $3 in November 2025 to $3.64 per gallon this November, according to AAA, the surging price of diesel is what is impacting the cost of nearly all goods for Americans.

GOOGLE'S NEW AI SHOPPING CART TRACKS DEALS ACROSS STORES

Tariffs are another potential source of price pressure. A New York Fed analysis found that about 26% of tariff increases from 2025 had been passed on to consumer prices. Retailers may also respond to higher costs by raising prices or reducing package sizes.

Gauri said some retailers have done both, a practice known as shrinkflation.

"The package size is getting smaller, even though the price might be the same," he said. "You’re shaving off, let’s say, 10% of the product."

Gauri said Black Friday promotions now often begin during Thanksgiving week and run through Cyber Monday, giving shoppers more time to compare prices online and in stores. The shift from doorbusters that once drew shoppers to stores before dawn the Friday after Thanksgiving means consumers can now research deals, order products and arrange for pickup or delivery.

To make sure a discount is worthwhile, Gauri recommended using price-tracking websites and Amazon’s price-history feature to check what an item has cost in recent months. 
"Consumers tend to overspend sometimes because they do not remember what an item previously cost," he said.

He also advised shoppers to compare prices across retailers and check each store’s price-matching policy before making a major purchase. Some retailers exclude Black Friday specials from those policies, he said.

Gauri cautioned that Black Friday is not always the best time to shop.

"For cellphones, Black Friday doesn’t get you anything special," he said, adding that the best deals on phones or plans often come in October, around new product launches and carrier promotions.

Still, shoppers may find Cyber Week discounts useful for stocking up on everyday essentials.

Adobe Analytics projects online sales of clothing basics will run 210% above the September average, while personal hygiene products will be up 150%. Baby products, pet supplies and household cleaning items are also expected to see a boost.

With budgets under pressure, Gauri advised shoppers to set a spending limit before heading into the holiday sales.

item.title: Pregnant inmate escapes in New Mexico prison transport SUV during Whataburger stop
item.description: Pregnant inmate Rebecca Taylor escaped a New Mexico corrections vehicle during a Whataburger stop in Albuquerque following a prenatal appointment.
item.content:encoded:
A search is underway for a pregnant inmate who escaped in a New Mexico corrections vehicle during a stop for food at Whataburger, authorities said on Thursday.

Rebecca Taylor, 26, escaped from custody on the way to the Western New Mexico Correctional Facility in Grants following a prenatal appointment on Wednesday morning, according to the New Mexico Corrections Department.

Taylor was incarcerated on multiple theft and burglary charges.

"Please use caution, and do not attempt to approach her. Wanted individuals can be unpredictable and may react unexpectedly if approached or confronted," the corrections department said.

TENNESSEE INMATE CONVICTED OF MURDER ESCAPES FROM PRISON, STEALS PICKUP TRUCK, MANHUNT UNDERWAY: OFFICIALS

She was last seen wearing a prison jumpsuit.

Three officers were transporting Taylor and another incarcerated woman back from their prenatal appointments when the group stopped for food in Albuquerque, officials said, according to KOAT.

At about 11:35 a.m. on Wednesday, they stopped for Whataburger along 98th Street.

As the driver stepped out of the vehicle, Taylor unbuckled herself and climbed into the driver’s seat before driving away, the outlet reported. The other inmate was able to jump out of the car and is now back in custody.

Taylor was not restrained during transport because she was pregnant.

It was unclear where the other two officers were after the vehicle stopped for food.

The Dodge Journey SUV was later found in an Albuquerque neighborhood with only Taylor's orange jumpsuit inside the vehicle. She has not been seen since.

MISSOURI STATE HIGHWAY PATROL CAPTURES CONVICTED MURDERER WHO ESCAPED TENNESSEE PRISON

"The vehicle was later located by GPS in the area of Crestview Drive SW in Albuquerque. Taylor was not inside the vehicle when it was located," the corrections department said.

Officials said it remains an active and ongoing multi-agency search.

item.title: Trump mourns Florida detective killed by suspected drunk driver on Thanksgiving
item.description: President Donald Trump paid tribute to Palm Beach County Detective Alan Smith, a bomb squad expert killed in a wrong-way crash on I-95 on Thanksgiving.
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump paid tribute Thursday to a Florida sheriff's detective killed in a wrong-way crash involving a suspected drunk driver on Thanksgiving morning.

The Palm Beach County Sheriff's Office identified the fallen officer as Detective Alan Smith, who had served with the department for nearly 20 years.

Smith, who specialized in explosives-related investigations, was fatally struck by a wrong-way driver on Interstate 95 early Thursday morning, according to the sheriff's office.

"It is with profound sadness and heavy hearts that we announce the devastating loss [of] our own, Detective Alan Smith," the department said in a statement.

DRUNK WRONG-WAY DRIVER KILLED MASS TROOPER AFTER 9 DRINKS AT BAR, DA REPORT SAYS

Speaking Thursday during an event at Mar-a-Lago, Trump paid his respects to the family of the fallen officer, whom he described as "highly respected."

"I just want to pay my respects to the family of a great police officer, an expert at bombs and explosives, who was killed today in an automobile accident while on duty," Trump said.

Trump described the crash as "horrific," saying the other driver had been traveling in the wrong direction on Interstate 95.

"It was a drunk driver. Really drunk driver," Trump said. "He was going on the opposite side of the highway, if you can believe it. And so it's a terrible thing that happened."

The Florida Highway Patrol arrested Raul Jonathan Espinoza Martinez, 37, Thursday afternoon at St. Mary's Medical Center in West Palm Beach.

SUSPECT IN DEADLY PHILADELPHIA POLICE AMBUSH FACES 76 CHARGES, ORDERED HELD WITHOUT BAIL

Troopers were joined by members of the Palm Beach County Sheriff's Office, who placed Martinez in the same handcuffs carried by Smith.

Martinez is expected to be booked into the Palm Beach County Jail once he is released from the hospital. He faces multiple charges, including DUI manslaughter, vehicular homicide, aggravated battery, aggravated battery on a law enforcement officer and driving with a suspended or revoked license.

Authorities said Martinez has been arrested three times for DUI and that his driver's license had been revoked for 10 years, according to local outlet CBS12.

"This is a tragedy that shouldn't have happened," Florida Highway Patrol Maj. Kevin Strickland said. "He shouldn't have been driving a car at all, so part of our investigation is gonna determine how he was driving the car he was driving and how he got access to that vehicle."

ALLEGED DRUNKEN DRIVER WAS OVER 3 TIMES THE LIMIT WHEN HE KILLED NEWLY ENGAGED WOMAN DAYS AFTER JAIL RELEASE

Smith joined the Palm Beach County Sheriff's Office in January 2007 before becoming a member of its bomb squad in 2012 and graduating from the FBI Hazardous Devices School in September 2013.

He also served as a task force officer with the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF), specializing in explosives-related investigations.

Beyond his law enforcement career, Smith was a college professor and was working toward completing his doctoral degree, according to the sheriff's office.

He is survived by his wife, Jennifer, and their 14-year-old son, Alexander.

"Above all his professional and academic accomplishments, Alan's greatest pride was his family," the sheriff's office said.

THE FBI IS CHANGING HOW IT FIGHTS CRIME AND PROTECTS AMERICANS IN THEIR COMMUNITIES

Tributes poured in from across the country, including from FBI Director Kash Patel.

"Detective Smith was one of the FBI's own, having graduated from the FBI Hazardous Devices School in September 2013," Patel wrote on X, adding that Smith had "a long decorated career of service to this country."

"This is yet another reminder of the sacrifices our law enforcement make standing their posts even on holidays to keep us safe," he added. "Never forget them and their families. Our prayers are with Detective Smith's wife and 14 year old son, as well as the colleagues he leaves behind."

Rep. Byron Donalds, R-Fla., Florida's governor-elect, also reacted to Smith's death, calling the news "devastating."

"This is a sober and heartbreaking reminder of the dangers that our brave law enforcement officers face day in and day out as they risk everything to keep us safe," he posted on X.
